Medzhybizh New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. This is the newer of Medzhybizh's two Jewish cemeteries, a companion to the Old cemetery documented elsewhere in this collection, serving the town where the Baal Shem Tov, founder of Hasidism, lived from 1740 to 1760 and remains buried — his grave a popular pilgrimage destination in Hasidic circles to this day. Medzhybizh's Jewish community, organized by 1511, became one of the largest in Podolia by the early 17th century, survived the Khmelnytsky massacre of 1650, and peaked at about 6,040 people (73 percent) by 1897. During WWII, a ghetto established in autumn 1941 saw 1,000 prisoners executed on September 22, 1942.
